evidence_items.excerpt: The application constructs a file path using an unvalidated, user-controlled value from the 'BenchmarkTest00011' HTTP header. The header value is used as the parent directory for a 'java.io.File' object. The subsequent call to 'fileTarget.exists()' then discloses whether a file or directory exists at the path constructed by the attacker. An attacker can use directory traversal sequences (e.g., '../') in the header to probe the file system for the existence of arbitrary files or directories.
evidence_items.title: Path Traversal and Information Disclosure via HTTP Header

evidence_items.excerpt: Detected a potential path traversal. A malicious actor could control the location of this file, to include going backwards in the directory with '../'. To address this, ensure that user-controlled variables in file paths are sanitized. You may also consider using a utility method such as org.apache.commons.io.FilenameUtils.getName(...) to only retrieve the file name from the path.
reported_cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
